title: Vareniki
subtitle: potato dumplings with fried onion and sour cream
description: Thin dumplings filled with mashed potato, boiled and tossed in butter, served with sour cream and slowly fried onions.

steps.text: Make the dough: in a large bowl, mix 1 cup of the flour (keep the other 1/2 cup aside), a pinch of salt and the boiling water with a fork. Add 1 tablespoon melted butter and the egg yolk and keep mixing. Add the remaining flour and knead for about 2 minutes until smooth and pliable. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.

Make the filling: place the peeled, quartered potatoes in a large pot, cover with water, add a teaspoon of salt and boil until very soft. Drain and roughly mash. Add 1 teaspoon butter, the pepper and 1 teaspoon more salt, stir and cool.
Fry the thinly sliced onions in a little oil over low heat for about 20 minutes until golden and completely soft. Add 2 tablespoons to the filling.

Roll the dough out on a well-floured surface to about 2 mm thick. Cut 7 cm circles with a cutter or glass. Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of each circle, fold in half and pinch the edges closed. Keep on a well-floured plate or board until done (they can be frozen in a single layer, then stored in a bag).
Bring a large pot of water to the boil and season generously with about 2 tablespoons of salt. Boil 10 vareniki at a time until they float, plus one more minute.
Lift out with a slotted spoon into a deep bowl with cubes of cold butter. Repeat with the rest. Toss until the butter melts and coats the vareniki, and serve with sour cream and fried onion.
